races.name: Darlington Ra & Ellie Wake Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Recent winner (16f, Good) for Faye Bramley with 2W4P on similar ground, giving this horse the strongest form credentials in the race; a natural hold-up runner who will sit further back than ideal in a field this dominated by off-the-pace types, which slightly blunts his finishing power.

runners_data.name: Cadillac Ranch
runners_data.note: Lightly raced profile with just one recorded run on Good (a win) makes him genuinely unknown quantity for Miss Callwood (7); the "1PPP-P" string after that win is concerning and his style is unclassified, so it is hard to build a confident case for him despite that single Good-ground success.

runners_data.name: Credit Union
runners_data.note: Jessica Bedi runner who has finished outside the first ten in all four recorded runs (0W0P) and carries a "fades in finish" flag that is a serious concern over 2m4f; wears headgear (h) and true hold-up style means he needs a strong pace to deliver anything — conditions here don't obviously suit.

runners_data.name: Rock Armour
runners_data.note: David Thompson's runner is 95 days off the track and has a flat-race background (12 runs, 0W2P on Good), with his true instinct to race from the rear; the long absence plus the redistribution into midfield on the map means his best position is already compromised before the gate opens.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Adam Nicol's four-year-old has finished sixth in both hurdle starts (both 2m, Good) and has no form beyond that trip, so the step to 2m4f at Sedgefield is a significant ask; Ryan Mania is a capable northern jockey but there is little in the form to suggest a step forward is imminent.

runners_data.name: Datstheholyallofit
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes for Patrick Neville (T14: 2/7) — the confirmed lone front-runner who goes 4/4 on Good ground including a win over this distance; clearly set to make all and his recent form (44-12) shows progressive improvement, making him the pivotal shape-setting horse in this race.

runners_data.name: Orestina
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies mare who won over 2m (Flat/Sta) and has shown speed but her hurdles form reads 10-P since; returns after 44 days wearing a tongue-tie (t), and though she has Good-ground experience her true hold-up style placed in midfield on the map means she is unlikely to be as close to Datstheholyallofit as she might need to be.

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Mike Sowersby's four-year-old, ridden by Maggs (3), wears a hood (p) and has finished no higher than fourth in five starts (0W0P on Good, 10/15 sim-going record); consistent but uninspiring, and the deep hold-up style means she needs conditions to play perfectly for her to trouble the principals.

races.paceDynamic: Datstheholyallofit is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice hurdle and, with Brian Hughes in the saddle for an in-form Patrick Neville yard, he is almost certain to dictate from the front at a pace of his own choosing over 2m4f on Good ground at Sedgefield. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Genealogy, Credit Union, Rock Armour, Orestina, and Sweet Cicely all want to race from the back — meaning the pace Datstheholyallofit sets is unlikely to be challenged or pressured at any stage of the race. This field holds considerably more hold-up and midfield types than the race shape can naturally accommodate; of those, Genealogy (recent winner, strong form) and Orestina (a course-and-distance type) are most likely to secure the closest position to the pace in practice. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: a lone front-runner allowed to control tempo on Good ground at a track that suits relaxed, rhythm-based jumping favours a horse who can dictate and be ridden conservatively, with the main threat coming from any closer who can time a run to arrive at the last with momentum — this race shape is most kind to prominent-to-midfield types with a finishing kick, not deep hold-up horses who will need the pace to be strong enough to draw them in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Datstheholyallofit Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Datstheholyallofit bowls along in front at a fair but unhurried clip and none of the hold-up pack can close the gap from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Hughes sets a comfortable gallop, jumps well through the back straight, and kicks early in the straight before the backmarkers can mount a meaningful challenge; his Good-ground form (4/4 on the going) and clear front-running role make him the most likely beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Arrives In Time
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Datstheholyallofit is genuinely strong enough to soften him up in the closing stages and a hold-up horse can pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Genealogy, with his 2W4P record on similar going and a recent win, is best placed among the backmarkers to pounce if the leader ties up; the 2m4f trip at Sedgefield does ask a stamina question that could expose Datstheholyallofit late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grab Places
scenarios.trigger: If Cadillac Ranch or another runner pushed out of their natural role manages to track the leader more closely than expected and picks up the runner-up spot.
scenarios.body: Cadillac Ranch's unknown profile and the redistributed midfield types like Rock Armour could scramble for the places if the pace is moderate and the race is run in a bunch; this shape relies on horses racing partially out of role so its probability is capped accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Hold-Up Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Datstheholyallofit has a jumping blunder or is outpaced early and the race turns into a muddling affair that opens up for the hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine pace-maker operating, the race becomes a tactical lottery and deeper hold-up types like Credit Union or Sweet Cicely could sneak into contention, though their poor recent form makes this a low-confidence outcome.

watchPoints.text: Datstheholyallofit — watch whether Brian Hughes quickens early in the home straight before the backmarkers can close; if he jumps cleanly at the second-last, he is extremely difficult to reel in from off the pace.

Genealogy — monitor his position coming out of the back straight; if he is more than eight lengths off the pace at the top of the hill, the hold-up crowd will struggle to land a blow regardless of finishing pace on this Good ground.

Rock Armour — 95-day absence for a horse with a flat-racing background makes his jumping under pressure a genuine unknown; a stumble or hesitation at an early flight could compromise the whole race for any horse immediately behind him.

Cadillac Ranch — Miss Callwood's amateur claim could be significant in a race where margins are tight; watch how she positions the horse in the first half-mile given his completely unknown running style in a field this compact.

Orestina — the tongue-tie fitted for the first time in this yard is worth noting as a flag that connections suspect she is not giving her all at home; if she travels more smoothly than her recent hurdles form suggests, she could be the value danger in midfield.

races.name: Newts Rocket To The Top Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Daaris
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer by profile who has course-and-distance experience at Southwell and a sole win over similar trips; going is fine, but a 38-day absence and a form string that reads 73334 for Kevin & Lauren Frost suggests reliability rather than brilliance, and the slow pace may leave him with too much ground to make up.
runners_data.comment: Daaris has been knocking persistently on the door, placing third in three of his last five starts, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions with our rating putting him narrowly top of this field; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must finally convert.

runners_data.name: Character Testing
runners_data.note: Recent good-ground form (2nd and 4th latest two starts) is the most relevant in this field, Jamie Hamilton a strong booking and 13 days since last run keeps him sharp; naturally holds up but compact enough to slot into a tracking role if the field bunches, making him one of the more interesting pace-scenario crossover horses.
runners_data.comment: Consistent profile and has run over today's trip and going before, with a second in recent starts giving him solid claims here; the main risk is he remains winless in his last five and may again find one too good.

runners_data.name: Expert Analysis
runners_data.note: A 94-day break is the headline concern, and a form string of C580-P on hurdles tells its own story; the "fades in finish" flag and 0W0P on comparable going mean this is a watching brief for Sean Quinlan, who will need things to fall perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Expert Analysis does at least return with distance and going experience to call upon, though 94 days off the track and a taxing 164 lb burden make confidence hard to sustain.

runners_data.name: Hijo de La Luna
runners_data.note: Trainer Simon West with only 2 runners in 14 days, visor fitted, and 13 days since last run — the horse holds decent placed form on good going but is a true hold-up type displaced forward on the map because the rear is overcrowded; a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means its actual chance is tempered if it cannot settle into a genuine closing position.
runners_data.comment: Hijo de La Luna brings experience over today's trip and going, and a third three starts back hints at ability, though he remains winless in recent starts; fit off a 13-day break and carrying 160 lb, our rating of 92 makes him an interesting proposition at a mark of 88.

runners_data.name: Return With Gold
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Brian Hughes takes over on what is a lightly-raced 4-year-old for Ollie Pears who has shown modest placed form; with no pace rivals to challenge him, he sets the tempo entirely on his own terms, and that control is his biggest asset regardless of a modest OR of 85.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Return With Gold faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third two starts back offers slim encouragement, but 154 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been on good ground at 18f+, so dropping to 2m1f is a notable trip reduction for Callum Pritchard to manage; a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map slot, the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) is the most pronounced in the field, and the shorter trip combined with racing out of role makes this a difficult profile to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Yanka Blue has shown consistent placing ability — second last time out and second two starts back — though weight at 151 lb may test her, and she drops away sharply in the formbook beyond that promising recent pair.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: The "fades in finish" tag is a real concern in a race where positioning is everything; Jonathan England rides for Sam England, a yard with modest recent strike rate, and although there is a placed run on good going, the horse's natural rear-end style is compromised by the congested field — all of which points to a hard race to win.
runners_data.comment: Littletown Lad has run over today's trip and going before and shaped with promise when second last time out, though that unseating two starts back clouds his profile; winless in his last five starts and carrying 151 lb, he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Breaking Ground
runners_data.note: Three consecutive "fades in finish" flags make this one of the most straightforwardly difficult horses to back in this shape; Miss Becky Smith takes a 7lb claim which helps the weight, but a 57-day absence, poor recent form (50-086) and a true hold-up style squeezed into midfield by necessity all work against.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Breaking Ground faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going, and the 57-day break at least means she arrives fresh, though recent form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: A tongue-tie is fitted and the yard (Mike Sowersby, 0/3 in 14 days) gives little encouragement; the horse has a moderate recent record with a pulled-up run included, and Charlie Maggs' 3lb claim softens the burden slightly, but racing out of its natural hold-up position at a modest pace over a trip its form suggests may be sharp enough is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up on one of those occasions, Red Trail is hard to fancy from her recent profile, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Scopic
runners_data.note: The lowest OR in the field at 59 and a form string of 6-8P6 with hood and tongue-tie fitted; Ben Haslam sends him here 39 days fresh but the sim-going figures (4/4, 0W0P) and redistribution out of a true hold-up role into a midfield slot make this a very difficult profile to make a case for in this company.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement despite being yet to win in his last four starts, Scopic returns after 39 days carrying 145 lb, and with limited form to go on, there remains plenty to find out about this gelding.

races.paceDynamic: Return With Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead, Brian Hughes can dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground at Sedgefield. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the race into a tactical affair where position off the final bend matters enormously over 2m1f. With the vast majority of the field being natural hold-up horses — Hijo de La Luna, Yanka Blue, Littletown Lad, Breaking Ground, Red Trail and Scopic all redistributed from the rear because they cannot all occupy their natural position — the field will bunch in midfield and early movers from that group will be best placed. The field contains far more hold-up types than the track map can accommodate at the rear; of those, Hijo de La Luna and Yanka Blue, both with genuine front-of-midfield pace, are most likely to press closest to Return With Gold in practice. This race shape — a single uncontested leader, moderate pace, congested midfield — strongly favours the horse who travels smoothest in the first half and picks up decisively from a prominent or tracking position once jumps are cleared.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Return With Gold Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Return With Gold bowls along uncontested and the pace never quickens enough to stretch the field.
scenarios.body: Hughes dictates every yard at a rhythm that suits his mount, and a lack of genuine pressure means the leader's stamina reserves stay intact to the last flight; a horse that can track the leader's sectionals and strike from second or third is ideally placed to collar or chase him home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse who travels into a prominent pitch off the steady pace makes a decisive move two out.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield means a horse who naturally rides handier than mapped can slip into a stalking role and pick off the leader in the straight; the modest tempo means stamina is not the issue, pure tactical sharpness is.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types aggressively seeks a forward position early, injecting an unplanned surge and stretching the field.
scenarios.body: A quicker mid-race gallop would expose horses who have been shuffled back against their will and reward the single genuine front-runner who is already in rhythm; horses with any proven form at a stronger pace would benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls so slowly that a cavalry charge develops from the final flight, giving genuine rear-runners a slim window.
scenarios.body: This requires most of the field to be flat and the bunched midfield to fail to quicken, opening a gap for a horse finishing late; given the redistributed nature of the supposed hold-up contingent, the chance of a true closer winning is structurally diminished.

watchPoints.text: Return With Gold — watch whether Brian Hughes settles immediately into a controlled lead or gets too far in front; if he opens a gap of more than four lengths by the third flight, the race may be run at a true crawl that sets up a sprint finish he could easily lose.

Hijo de La Luna and Yanka Blue — both are true hold-up types who may refuse to be restrained into an unnatural midfield position, creating an unplanned surge in the first half mile that scrambles the anticipated single-pace scenario.

Character Testing — Jamie Hamilton's ability to manoeuvre from a hold-up base into a prominent tracking role at the first flight will be the critical early move; if he misses that slot in a 10-runner field, he faces a compromised trip.

Expert Analysis — monitor the market ahead of the off; a 94-day absence with a fading finish tendency means any significant support would warrant attention, but a drifting price would confirm the concern around fitness and recent form.

Breaking Ground and Littletown Lad — both carry "fades in finish" flags and are mapped out of their natural positions; if either is seen pushing wide early or pulling for position, it signals a chaotic mid-race phase that could collapse the controlled-pace scenario entirely.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Delpotro
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Charlie Longsdon, ridden by the in-form Sean Bowen — 12 from 15 in similar going and a 59-day break shouldn't blunt him on Good turf; the OR 105 ceiling makes him the class act in this field and Bowen's tactical read will be the key variable.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Delpotro has run over today's trip and going and our rating of 108 marks him out as a leading danger at the weights; the main concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts and a 59-day absence adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish yard operating at 2/10 in the 14-day window (warm form), and Ian Power takes over at age 9 — the horse's consistent prominent racing style suits this trip, having placed 2nd and 3rd at today's sort of distance on Good; 43 days off is routine.|
runners_data.comment: Thank You Blue arrives winless in his last five starts but has shown consistent placing ability, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; at 165 lb he faces a stiff ask, but our rating of 115 marks him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Fiskardo
runners_data.note: Recent winner (1st, 16f, Good) and a strong 5/7 sim-going record — Shane Fenelon claims 5lbs which is a meaningful aid at OR 102; only 9 days between runs, which for a 6-year-old on Good ground raises a mild freshness question, but Mickey Bowen's yard is in fine recent form (3/15).|
runners_data.comment: Fiskardo showed a tidy mix of consistency and ability when winning and finishing second and third in recent starts, and he returns on a quick nine-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going before; the burden of 165 lb is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Wherearethejudges
runners_data.note: A long 193-day absence is the defining concern here — all three known runs were on Soft, so today's Good ground is an unknown quantity; Callum Bewley takes over for a yard that is 3/6 in 14 days, suggesting the trainer is confident, but the fitness deficit is hard to overlook.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up most recently, Wherearethejudges carries 163 lb on his return from 193 days off, which is the key question here; he has run over today's trip before, but a rating of 96 ranking him sixth of nine underlines the size of the task.

runners_data.name: Wudya
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going profile (13/15 on Good, 2 wins, 5 places) and the tongue-strap suggests a horse that needs to be settled — Danny McMenamin is an able partner; at OR 100 and prominent in style, the consistent fourth-placings suggest a place rather than a win is the likely outcome.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Wudya nonetheless shaped with promise when fourth two runs back and again three runs back, and has run over today's trip and going; the chief concern is a hefty 163 lb on her back.

runners_data.name: Tom Creen
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old off a 140-day break, with a form string of 27P3U — the unseating is a jumping concern at Sedgefield's fences; likely to struggle to secure his preferred front-running slot against younger rivals and may be eased back from his natural position organically.|
runners_data.comment: Tom Creen has experience over today's trip and going, and his third two starts back offers some encouragement, but he is winless in his last five starts, returns after 140 days off, and unseated last time out — all giving pause on his claims from stall.

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby sends this out just 13 days after its last run, which signals confidence — a 14/15 sim-going record is the most impressive in the field, and hold-up style suits this scenario perfectly; the step up to 2m3½f from habitual 17-18f efforts is the key distance test to monitor.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Clean Getaway faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going before and comes back quickly after 13 days, and he carries 149 lb.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Wears a visor, and recent form shows a placed effort (2nd, 20f, Soft) two runs back — the 7/15 sim-going record and OR 86 leave him needing the race to go entirely his way; Jamie Hamilton is a capable partner but the yard is 0/9 in the 14-day window, a cold statistic.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Huit Reflets faces a stiff ask at 149 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going and does show some consistency, finishing second twice in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's runner has a 15/15 similar-going record — every qualifying run has been in similar conditions, a strong fit — but the form string ends with a pulled-up and no wins in the last five; at OR 83, the lowest-rated runner, and consistent prominent racing hasn't converted into victories.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Applejack Poet's case is not helped by a pulled-up effort last time, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 40-day break carrying 146 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Delpotro, Fiskardo, and Tom Creen all want to lead, guaranteeing a strong gallop from the outset over 2m3½f on Good ground at Sedgefield — a track where stamina is routinely tested even at fair pace. With three genuine front-runners contesting for the same real estate, there will be early friction and pressure that ensures no tactical race: the fractions will be honest or better from the first fence. The field holds more front-running types than can all secure a clear lead, with Delpotro (Sean Bowen, class edge) and Fiskardo (recent winner, good record in similar going) the most likely pair to actually dictate at the front, while Tom Creen — at 11 and carrying 193 days' layoff — is the most likely to be squeezed back from his preferred position. This race shape heavily favours prominent-to-midfield horses with proven stamina and the tactical nous to settle just off the war between the leaders, striking when those front-runners tire in the final two fences.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Rewards Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way battle for the lead burns the principals out, allowing prominent/midfield horses to pick up the pieces from 2 out.
scenarios.body: Delpotro, Fiskardo, and Tom Creen push each other hard across the first circuit, burning petrol at a rate that will leave the genuine stayers in the pack with a clear route to pounce; the final hill at Sedgefield becomes a stamina examination that the hold-up and prominent types handle better than the battle-weary leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the primary front-runners — most likely Delpotro with Sean Bowen in the saddle — establishes a measured lead and idles rather than blasts, controlling tempo and kicking clear from 3 out.
scenarios.body: Bowen's tactical intelligence could allow Delpotro to dictate at a sensible clip, using a good jumping round to conserve energy; at OR 105, Delpotro has the class ceiling to hold off challengers if the pace battle resolves with him clear and unflustered by 4 out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Grind, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal end-to-end, wiping out all prominent horses and leaving the race to the deepest stayers to come from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Clean Getaway's strong recent activity (13 days ago, 14/15 sim-going record) and consistent form around 17-18f suggest it could be competitive if the trip stretches the others; Wherearethejudges, a 193-day absentee, is a wildcard with unknown fitness but capable form when right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Scrambles Form
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion between Delpotro, Fiskardo, Tom Creen, and the four jostling runners triggers interference at the 2nd-3rd fence cluster, with potential fallers or checked horses reshaping the race entirely.
scenarios.body: At a tight track like Sedgefield with a compressed field, early traffic incidents are a genuine risk when multiple runners all seek the same inside position; any horse that avoids trouble and jumps cleanly into clear daylight could be dragged into an unexpected position of advantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch the early skirmish between Delpotro, Fiskardo, and Tom Creen for the lead — the most physically vulnerable moment is the 2nd fence cluster when all three may arrive simultaneously, creating a genuine risk of interference or a jumping error under pressure.

Fiskardo running just 9 days after its last race could show signs of tiredness in the final half-mile if the pace proves relentless — Shane Fenelon's inexperience at this level adds an element of uncertainty if things get tactical quickly.

Wherearethejudges returns after 193 days entirely on Soft ground — if the Good surface doesn't suit or the fitness isn't there, an early exit is plausible; monitor closely in the preliminaries and at the first fence for any signs of reluctance.

Clean Getaway's stamina for 2m3½f is unproven — its entire recent form is over 17-18f, so watch whether Joe Williamson rides with confidence from the back or settles for a place as the trip extends into the final circuit.

The 4-way battle for prominent positions (Thank You Blue and Wudya joining the three confirmed leaders) means traffic at 2-3 out is a meaningful risk — any horse finding clear daylight on the outside at that point could appear to "fly" purely due to the compression of rivals on the inner.|

races.name: Warm-Flo Hot To Trot Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Machete Beach
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins from last four starts over 2m-2m2f on Good; Snowden's yard is 2/4 in the past 14 days, Sheehan is a strong partner for leaders, and 44 days off the track looks unlikely to blunt his pace-setting ability.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in good heart, Machete Beach has won twice in his last five starts with a second last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the 44-day break is the one query, but his rating of 120 makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up mare wearing tongue-tie and cheekpieces, 41 days between runs and trainer Sam England is 0/4 in the past fortnight — her two wins from 15 Good-ground starts shows she can handle the conditions but the pace shape here does not set up naturally for her style.
runners_data.comment: Glory And Honour landed a win three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with our rating of 120 marking him as a leading threat — the concern is a seventh last time out that he must put behind him here.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner who ran well at up to 2m4f; the 66-day absence warrants monitoring but Candlish is 2/10 in the 14-day window and his Good-ground record (7/10 placed or better) suggests the conditions suit — his natural hold-up style is marginally better served than the other rear-runners given his recent winning momentum.
runners_data.comment: Saint Polo arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, making him a serious threat at the head of the market; the main concern is a 66-day absence since that last success.

runners_data.name: Jolie Coeur Allen
runners_data.note: Solid recent form (second and fourth) and won over 17f on Good 41 days ago, but his natural preference for holding up off the pace is compromised today — placed at midfield on the map because the race lacks room for multiple rear-runners, meaning he must race forward of his comfort zone and his STYLE_FIT of 0.94 flags a structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner five starts back, Jolie Coeur Allen brings distance and going experience alongside a rating of 107 to make her a genuine threat here; the main concern is the 41-day absence.

runners_data.name: Scots Poet
runners_data.note: Three wins from 15 Good-ground starts and ran well here recently, but at 10 years old and carrying blinkers/tongue-tie, his genuine hold-up profile is similarly squeezed by the race shape — forced into a midfield berth he does not naturally seek, with Whillans 0/8 in the last fortnight adding another soft flag.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures and carrying a hefty 158 lb, Scots Poet is hard to fancy at the weights, and an unseated rider last time out does nothing to boost confidence, though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Fine Point
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer who won on this course 13 days ago and has an excellent Good-ground record (13/15 starts); Mania is a sharp judge at Sedgefield and Fine Point's ability to sit just off the leader is a genuine tactical asset, though he will need Machete Beach to crack to take full advantage.
runners_data.comment: Fine Point unseated last time out and ranks last on our figures in a six-runner field, making him hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Machete Beach is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, Gavin Sheehan can dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front across Sedgefield's 2m1f trip on Good ground. Fine Point (P) will press forward to track but lacks the authority to force Machete Beach off his own rhythm, meaning the early tempo is likely to be honest rather than frenetic — a pace entirely within Machete Beach's control. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can absorb: Jolie Coeur Allen and Scots Poet are genuine rear-end operators who are mapped to midfield only because they have nowhere further back to go, meaning they will effectively race out of their natural role today. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a manageable gallop — overwhelmingly favours the front-running profile and those able to track closely, while true hold-up runners are structurally disadvantaged by the lack of a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Machete Beach Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach is allowed to roll along at his own pace and Fine Point cannot sustain a challenge from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Machete Beach controls the race throughout, never over-exerting himself in the early stages, and his recent winning form over similar trips on Good ground (two wins in last four) makes him the standout beneficiary of an uncontested lead; Sheehan simply needs to time the kick off the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fine Point or a horse tracking closely exploits any jumping error or flat spot from Machete Beach in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Fine Point, fresh from a win 13 days ago and prominent by nature, is ideally positioned to pounce if the leader makes a mistake or ties up on the run-in; Ryan Mania has the course form and experience at Sedgefield to time a challenge perfectly from close range.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong and the race is run at a searching gallop that sets up a late finish.
scenarios.body: Saint Polo is the most convincing of the hold-up types given back-to-back wins and strong Good-ground form, and would be best placed to pick up the pieces; however, Jolie Coeur Allen and Scots Poet are both racing structurally out of their preferred role, which constrains confidence in this shape materialising.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Pace Creates Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach meets a fence badly or is forced wide early, disrupting the expected rhythm and causing a muddled tempo.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristic jumping error or interference could compress the field and hand momentum to Glory And Honour, who has winning course form at this trip and handles Good ground, though her age (10) and T14 blank give pause.

watchPoints.text: Machete Beach's jumping must be monitored — if he makes a significant error at any of the early hurdles, Fine Point is perfectly positioned to capitalise and the entire race shape shifts.

Scots Poet and Jolie Coeur Allen are both being forced to race closer to the pace than ideal; watch whether either becomes restless or unruly in the early stages, which could inject unwanted pace and stretch Machete Beach's lead.

Glory And Honour showed a win here in similar conditions but her trainer's 0/4 fortnight and her age suggest any fitness shortfall will be exposed on the run from the last — watch if she fades quickly after looking a threat turning in.
Fine Point's 13-day turnaround is notably quick for a five-year-old hurdler; watch his jumping sharpness early to assess whether the quick return has left him fresh or flat.

races.name: Bodhi Bespoke Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Getaway Vic
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and architect of the pace here; seven runs on identical Good ground yielding 2W6P is strong confirmation of going suitability, and Mickey Bowen's charge has placed twice over the 23f trip this season — at 168lbs he carries the joint-topweight burden but his Sedgefield experience is the key tactical asset.
runners_data.comment: Getaway Vic has been placing consistently, finishing second two starts back and second three starts back, and his experience on today's going is a clear asset; the main concern is a 49-day absence that leaves his current sharpness an open question.

runners_data.name: Maggies Boy
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan partners a genuine hold-up horse returning on 57 days off, and his 12W6P sim-going record across 15 runs flags strong surface compatibility; won over 21f on Good and placed over 24f, so the trip is within range, but he needs a proper gallop to set up a late challenge that this race shape may not deliver.
runners_data.comment: Maggies Boy shaped well when second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with that experience counting in his favour here; the 57-day absence is the one query, but he carries 161 lb off a mark of 98 with plenty to recommend him.

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: Prominent-running nine-year-old trained by Sam England who won over 26f on Good at his last start and has the widest range of Good-ground course form in the field at 13W7P from 15 runs; sits directly behind Getaway Vic in the natural race shape and is the most likely horse to apply sustained pressure if the pace drifts.
runners_data.comment: Jeteye returns off a 41-day break having won last time out, with two victories in his last five starts and experience of today's going working in his favour; the main concern is whether the 158 lb burden blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Brian Ellison whose most productive form came on Soft ground — only 6W1P from 11 Good-ground runs — and his recent string of 16th, pulled up, 4th gives grounds for caution; the step up to 3m2½f on Good is a combination that his form book has not fully endorsed.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up two starts back and unplaced the run before that make him hard to recommend, and our rating of 82 ranks him sixth of seven here; he has run over today's going before and returns after 41 days, but the recent profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Uncle Al
runners_data.note: Returned just 13 days ago for Jessica Bedi and is the freshest horse in the field on a quick turnaround; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, his position on the map understates how deep he is likely to race, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that a controlled front-running shape does not play to his strengths — his one win at 24f on Good is nonetheless relevant if he gets cover.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Uncle Al has shown he can find the frame but a pulled up and an unseated flank that sequence; ranked last of seven on our figures, he looks hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Jo Arengeot Bey AA
runners_data.comment: Jo Arengeot Bey AA arrives on the back of a second last time out and a win three starts back, showing he retains ability on his favoured going; the main risk is that pull-up two starts back, which must give some pause.

runners_data.name: Croagh Patrick
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes on an 11-year-old veteran whose natural hold-up style means he will race further back than the map suggests; Gillian Boanas has had no runners in the past 14 days and this is Croagh Patrick's first run in 61 days — 0W2P on Good across sim-going runs and a recent record of pulled up and two question marks over 26f trips make it hard to build a case beyond survival value.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up on his most recent outing 61 days ago, Croagh Patrick faces a stiff task off 142 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and that second two starts back offers some encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Getaway Vic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 3m2½f chase and will stride into an uncontested lead from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop on Good ground at Sedgefield. With no genuine rival to pressure him early, he can dictate every fraction and control tempo through the long back straight, giving him the classic advantage of racing on his own terms across a stamina-sapping trip. Jeteye and Jo Arengeot Bey will look to track him prominently, but neither has the natural speed to go and take it to Getaway Vic if he quickens the pace at any point. This shape — an unchallenged leader controlling fractions over a staying trip on a fair surface — squarely favours prominent-to-front-running types with the jumping accuracy and stamina to capitalise on a set pace rather than closers who need a truly searching gallop to be dragged into contention. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear with purpose: Uncle Al and Croagh Patrick are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice they are most likely to find themselves mid-to-rear with limited scope to deliver a decisive late challenge unless the race is genuinely run to suit them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Getaway Vic Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Getaway Vic bowls along unchallenged at a measured pace and his jumping holds up over the fences.
scenarios.body: Getaway Vic sets fractions entirely to his own liking, conserving energy through the middle section before asserting from the final fence home; his seven sim-going runs of 2W6P on identical going underline his reliability in these conditions. Prominent trackers who travel fluently behind him are best placed to mount a challenge, but with no sustained pressure applied early, the leader's advantage is hard to claw back over 3m2½f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Him Down
scenarios.trigger: If Jeteye or Jo Arengeot Bey locks on to Getaway Vic's girth from halfway and tests his stamina through the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Getaway Vic's lead is neutralised if a prominent rival refuses to sit and instead keeps the race honest, turning it into a true test of staying power from three out; Jeteoe's three wins from 15 Good-ground runs and recent Sedgefield form make him the likelier danger. Jo Arengeot Bey's 24f win on Good ground also fits, and a sustained duel between the front two opens the door for a horse travelling sweetly in behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and a closer produces a sustained late run over the stamina test.
scenarios.body: Maggies Boy is the most credible hold-up threat here given his win at 24f on Good and Sean Quinlan's ability to produce horses late, though the modest tempo set by Getaway Vic makes a late scythe-through-the-field outcome genuinely unlikely. You Did's record on Good ground is mixed and Uncle Al, while a true hold-up type, carries the STYLE_FIT discount having been pushed out of his natural position — the scenario requires an unusual pace collapse to fully materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, unseats or the fences cause significant carnage that reshuffles the race entirely.
scenarios.body: A chase over 3m2½f always carries jumping risk, and any incident at the prominent horses reduces the race to a test of who stays upright; Croagh Patrick, an 11-year-old veteran, has the course craft to creep into contention if rivals fall away, though his 0W2P sim-going record tempers optimism. Maggies Boy and You Did, sitting off the pace, would also inherit ground in a messy race without having to pick up aggressively.

watchPoints.text: Getaway Vic's jumping accuracy is the pivotal factor — if he makes an early jumping error and surrenders his lead, the entire race shape collapses and hold-up types Maggies Boy and Uncle Al inherit a more genuinely competitive contest.

Uncle Al's 13-day turnaround is the shortest fresher interval in the field — watch for signs of fatigue from three out if Conor O'Farrell pushes forward earlier than expected to avoid traffic at the back.

Croagh Patrick's age (11) and 61-day absence make him an each-way jumping risk over the longer trip; Brian Hughes is skilled at placing older chasers, but a mistake at a fence could compromise multiple runners' positions in a small field.

If Jeteye moves upsides Getaway Vic on the final circuit rather than sitting in behind, the pace scenario shifts from controlled to competitive — Jonathan England's tactical choice at the top of the back straight is the key race-reading moment.

You Did's marginal Good-ground record (6/11) versus his better Soft form means conditions may not entirely suit; watch whether Patrick Wadge elects to hunt for a position nearer the pace rather than relying on a late run that this shape is unlikely to set up.

races.name: MW Civils & Groundworks Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Aimeric
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Jennie Candlish and Sean Quinlan, has form figures of 4-44 but all placed finishes on Good ground; 52 days off is not a concern and the 2m4f trip suits, though he has never won from as deep as his natural position suggests.
runners_data.comment: Aimeric has been knocking on the door with three consecutive fourths in recent starts, and his experience on today's going gives him a solid platform to go one better; the concern is that he has been winless in this recent sequence and may find the 168 lb he shoulders a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Socks Off
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning from 220 days off — a substantial absence that makes his fitness questionable; though shown on the lead as the only pace-setter, he is a natural hold-up horse redirected to the front by process of elimination, so his role-fit is weak and connections should be discounted in front-running shapes accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placer who has been third three times in recent starts, and our rating of 105 puts him right in contention, but 166 lb is a hefty burden and 220 days off the track is the key concern for a gelding yet to win in this recent spell.

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Donald McCain wearing tongue-tie; form includes three third-place finishes at 16f on Good ground, and the trip here is a slight stretch at 20f, though the consistent placings suggest he travels well and finishes honestly.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placer who has finished third on three occasions in recent starts, American Empire has run over today's going and arrives here on a competitive weight of 166 lb, with our rating of 99 marking him a leading danger; the main concern is that he remains yet to win in his last five outings.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's nine-year-old has an outstanding record on Good ground (all 15 similar-going runs have produced a placed finish) and comes here having won at 24f — the distance is ideal; shown in midfield as the map could not accommodate all hold-up types at the rear, but his true preference is to race patiently from the back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but did finish second three runs back and third four runs back, giving Indian Sunbird some each-way claims; he has run over today's trip and going, though 165 lb is a stiff ask and a 37-day absence adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: William Yeats
runners_data.note: Sam England's five-year-old had 140 days off and is fitted with a tongue-tie; most of his form comes on Soft ground (1W from 5 runs on similar) so the Good going here is a slight concern, and while the race map places him in midfield, he naturally wants to race held up and this surface switch may blunt his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in defeat of late with back-to-back thirds in his last two starts, and a winner five starts back, William Yeats has experience over today's trip and going; the 140-day absence is the one query, but his rating of 113 marks him as the clear class act here.

runners_data.name: Lipstick Traces
runners_data.note: Justin Landy's six-year-old has a fall in recent form (F) which warrants monitoring for jumping confidence; all form is on Good or Good-to-Soft ground so the surface is fine, and while shown in midfield by redistribution, she is a hold-up horse who needs a clean run to produce her best late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lipstick Traces does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a 44-day freshen-up may help, though she shoulders 164 lb as a mare rated 92 officially.

runners_data.name: Pepite De Saphir
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's mare wears a tongue-tie and has not registered a win across six similar-going runs, placing a ceiling on her ceiling; the map pushes her into midfield but she naturally races off the pace, and her record of 0W0P on comparable ground is a notable negative.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pepite De Saphir does show a second three starts back to suggest she retains ability, though a pulled-up run two starts back and 85 days off the track are questions she must answer under a hefty 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: David Thompson's five-year-old wears a hood and is partnered by a 5lb claimer (Joshua Thompson), which partially offsets his OR of 89; his best run was a third over 20f on Good going and while the redistribution places him in midfield, he is a hold-up type who can finish honestly if not buried in traffic.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Top Flight Century faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the third two starts back offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's six-year-old wears blinkers and tongue-tie and has two wins at 18-20f on Good ground from nine similar-going runs — the form is live; shown in midfield by redistribution but naturally a patient hold-up horse who has won when given a clear run, making him one of the more credible threats if the race develops into a late sprint.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying a hefty 157 lb, Makinbecon is hard to fancy on his latest sixth, though he has winning form in recent starts and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Lillistar
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's six-year-old comes back quickly after just 24 days and is ridden by Brian Hughes, the standout jockey booking in the race; recent form includes a fall and a pulled-up so jumping reliability is a concern, and while redistributed to midfield, she is a hold-up type whose best finishes have come over shorter trips than today's 2m4f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Lillistar has a tough task carrying 151 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and the 24-day break at least means she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Socks Off is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 10-runner handicap hurdle over 2m4f on Good ground at Sedgefield, though it is a redistributed horse racing out of its natural hold-up role — meaning the early tempo is likely to be modest and uncontested rather than genuinely pressured. With Socks Off setting a sustainable gallop unchallenged, this race is likely to develop into a slowly-run, bunched affair where the race is won in the closing stages rather than run as a true test of stamina. The field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Aimeric, American Empire, Indian Sunbird, William Yeats, Lipstick Traces, Pepite De Saphir, Top Flight Century, Makinbecon, and Lillistar all prefer to race off the pace — meaning the map cannot reflect their natural positions, and several (Indian Sunbird, William Yeats, Lipstick Traces, Pepite De Saphir, Top Flight Century, Makinbecon, Lillistar) have been redistributed to midfield simply because there is no room at the rear. The field holds far more natural hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate towards the back; of those, the ones most likely to secure a genuinely rearward berth are Aimeric and American Empire, as they are the only true hold-up runners not redistributed. A moderate, single-file gallop set by a reluctant front-runner strongly favours runners with a late, sharp finish — patient hold-up horses who can travel efficiently and produce a decisive effort at the final flight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Socks Off Dictates Modestly
scenarios.trigger: If Socks Off sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the field strings out conservatively before quickening late.
scenarios.body: Socks Off controls the pace without pressure and the race is effectively a sprint finish from 2 out, with the field bunched and finishing in a cluster; genuine hold-up horses who can switch off and finish sharply are advantaged.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace dips so low that the last two hurdles become the entire race, rewarding the horse with the sharpest turn of foot.
scenarios.body: The dawdling tempo collapses the field into a mass finish, making positional sense irrelevant and handing the advantage to horses with a clean, economical jumping style and a powerful late surge; horses naturally suited to a flat-track sprint finish over hurdles come to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed prominent type gets closer to the pace than expected and uses that position to outstay rivals from the front.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses shuffled back, a runner who manages to slot into a tracking position behind Socks Off gains a significant positional edge and can dictate terms from 3 out; Indian Sunbird's strong record on Good ground (15/15 similar-going runs in frame) makes it particularly suited to capitalising on that positional advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Blocked
scenarios.trigger: If the field clusters so tightly behind a slow pace that hold-up horses face traffic and the race is won by a horse who was never more than three lengths off the leader.
scenarios.body: Congestion in a slowly-run race with ten runners and no genuine pace creates a pocket of trouble for horses trying to switch and pick up late; a runner who travels well without needing daylight and can produce a clean jump at the last inherits the race by default.

watchPoints.text: Socks Off is returning from 220 days off and is a hold-up horse redirected to the lead — watch whether he actually commits to front-running or drifts back, as that would leave the race effectively paceless and distort every scenario.

Makinbecon has blinkers and tongue-tie and two wins on this ground and trip — watch for him to be ridden with more intent than his mapped midfield position suggests, as he may be able to secure a better-than-expected berth early.

With nine of ten runners naturally wanting to race hold-up and the field redistribution bunching them into midfield, watch for severe congestion and switching issues from 4 out, particularly affecting Lipstick Traces and Lillistar who need daylight to deliver their best.

Brian Hughes on Lillistar represents the most significant jockey upgrade in the race — watch how he manages her jumping after recent falls, as Hughes's horsemanship is likely to be tested early and could determine whether she completes competitively.

Indian Sunbird's all-15 placed record on Good going is the standout form statistic — watch whether James Best angles for a closer position than the hold-up map suggests, as a forward move from the gate could make that going record decisive.

races.name: Bodhi Creative Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: You Be Lucky Jean
runners_data.comment: Sole recent start ended in victory, and she has run over today's trip and going, giving her a fitness edge to weigh against 96 days off; at the head of our ratings, You Be Lucky Jean looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Youlooklikeyourmum
runners_data.comment: Unraced and entirely unexposed, Youlooklikeyourmum makes her debut carrying 156 lb and represents a complete unknown with every improvement still ahead of her.

runners_data.name: Arc Kunoichi
runners_data.comment: Unraced and entirely unexposed, Arc Kunoichi makes her debut carrying 153 lb, with nothing in the book yet but plenty unknown and potentially untapped.

runners_data.name: Cumnock
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Cumnock steps into the unknown here carrying 153 lb, but with no form to weigh up she remains a fascinating unknown quantity and could be anything.

runners_data.name: Grey Day
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Grey Day arrives with her record a blank slate and plenty of scope for improvement; carrying 153 lb, she is one to watch as connections look to get her off the mark.

runners_data.name: Megatothemax
runners_data.comment: Megatothemax shaped with real promise on her most recent start, finishing third, and has experience over today's trip to call on; rated 102 and ranked second in the field, she looks a leading danger, though the 86-day absence is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Reverse Charge
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Reverse Charge is a filly yet to score who arrives at the track as a fascinating unknown; carrying 153 lb, she merits close inspection as connections unveil her for the first time.

runners_data.name: Tottie's Moon
runners_data.comment: Tottie's Moon has run over today's trip and going and, rated 92 in a field of nine, she shapes as a leading contender on form profile, though her fifth last time out and a lengthy 78-day break are the main questions connections must answer.

runners_data.name: True Measure
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, True Measure returns from a 177-day absence carrying 153 lb, and though yet to win in recent starts, her light campaign leaves plenty of scope for better.
